bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42501404 (freeradius-server): Global-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target fuzzer_tacacs [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42501404
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / exact staged vulnerable workspace / staged poc bytes
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` while `fuzzer_tacacs` decoded the exact staged 79-byte witness (sha256 `71d6b9c6e021b03529a022697745d16e7b9e9fb942fdb42ff3cfc6b576ec5bad`) on vulnerable commit `10bc205ff66c31933260c298e29efc9981631877`. The header bytes `c0 02 20 ff 20 20 20 20 00 00 00 43` make this an unencrypted TACACS Authorization RESPONSE with even `seq_no == 0x20` and a 67-byte body. Inside that body, `arg_cnt = 9`, `data_len = 9`, and the first three argument lengths are `0`, `10`, and `33`; after the 9-byte `Data` field, exactly 43 argument-payload bytes remain, so those first three lengths already consume the whole remaining payload and the third argument still fits exactly. Vulnerable `tacacs_decode_args()` therefore reaches the third 33-byte argument `DATa*0x                \xff\xff\xff \xff\xff    `, case-insensitive dictionary lookup resolves `DATa` to TACACS attribute `Data`, and `fr_pair_value_from_str()` parses the value with `FR_TYPE_OCTETS`. `fr_value_box_from_str()` strips the `0x` prefix and passes the remaining 26 bytes, which still contain raw `0xff`, into `fr_base16_decode_nstd()`. In the base16 helper, `fr_is_base16_nstd()` evaluates `alphabet[(uint8_t)c]` with `c == 0xff`; because `fr_base16_alphabet_decode_mc` has only 255 elements, index 255 reads one byte past the global table and ASan reports the crash at line 53. The staged patch does not change the base16 helper; it blocks this exact witness earlier by pre-validating the TACACS argument-length vector and rejecting the malformed packet before `tacacs_decode_args()` begins parsing.

source.description: First scored project statement on the crashing path that consumes the TACACS reply dispatch key and selects the Authorization RESPONSE body parser.
source.value_from: The staged PoC header is `c0 02 20 ff 20 20 20 20 00 00 00 43`: the enclosing `switch (pkt->hdr.type)` has already selected `FR_TAC_PLUS_AUTHOR`, and this predicate consumes the even `seq_no == 0x20` that routes parsing into the Authorization RESPONSE layout.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: The mixed-case base16 decode table is only 255 bytes long even though later code indexes it with `(uint8_t)c`, so byte value `0xff` has no in-bounds slot.
root_cause.note: This is the load-bearing bug for the reproduced crash: once the accepted third `Data` argument sends a raw `0xff` byte into base16 decoding, index 255 is out of bounds regardless of the later 32-byte argument lengths that the staged patch rejects earlier.
operands: all remaining arg_list[] lengths from p fit before end

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. A raw `0xff` byte from the accepted `Data` argument is converted to index 255 and read from the too-short base16 decode table.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `global-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` here; the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of global `fr_base16_alphabet_decode_mc` defined in `src/lib/util/base16.c:75` with size 255.

tainted_value_origin.description: This materializes the exact 33-byte third argument that later resolves to TACACS `Data` and feeds the crashing octets/base16 parse.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: After the 9-byte `Data` field and the preceding 10-byte second-argument payload, the next 33 bytes are `44 41 54 61 2a 30 78 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 ff ff ff 20 ff ff 20 20 20 20`.

parser_admitted.description: The header bytes select the TACACS Authorization path and then satisfy the even-sequence-number reply predicate, so the decoder enters the Authorization RESPONSE body parser.

arg_payload_cursor.description: After the 9-byte `Data` field is consumed, `p` points at the first argument payload byte and only 43 payload bytes remain for all declared arguments.

third_argument_admitted.description: When the loop reaches `i = 2`, the first two lengths have advanced `p` by 10 bytes and `arg_list[2] == 33` still satisfies `p + 33 == end`, so the crashing third argument is accepted before any later 32-byte lengths are consulted.

evidence_limitations: `trace_feedback.json` was present and its concrete source/root-cause corrections were incorporated. `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so no instrumentation was added and every step is grounded only in the staged vulnerable source plus the saved Stage 01 crash artifacts.

Stage 02 did not run the fixed image. The staged patch source-groundedly blocks this exact witness earlier by rejecting the malformed TACACS argument vector, but the downstream base16 helper in the crashing stack is unchanged in this diff.

ASan prints the inline helper path as `src/freeradius-devel/util/base16.h:53`; the matching staged vulnerable checkout contains the same `fr_is_base16_nstd` body at `src/lib/util/base16.h:53`, included by `src/lib/util/base16.c`.

fine_trace.note: Control dispatch. The header type byte is `0x02`, so parsing enters the `FR_TAC_PLUS_AUTHOR` branch.
Source. Within the TACACS Authorization branch, the even sequence number `0x20` satisfies `packet_is_author_response(pkt)` and selects the Authorization RESPONSE body layout.
This consumes `arg_cnt == 9`, checks only that the 9-byte argument-length table fits, and advances `p` past the length bytes `00 0a 21 20 20 20 20 20 20`.
This consumes `data_len == 9`, validates and copies only that 9-byte field, and advances `p` to the first argument payload byte. Exactly 43 argument-payload bytes remain after this point.

At `i = 0` the zero-length entry is skipped, and at `i = 1` the 10-byte second entry advances `p` by 10 bytes. When the loop reaches `i = 2`, `arg_list[2] == 33` still satisfies `p + 33 == end`, so the third argument is admitted; the later 32-byte lengths are not consulted before the crash path is already in flight.
The accepted third argument is materialized as the 33-byte string `DATa*0x                \xff\xff\xff \xff\xff    `.

The scan stops at `*`, terminates the name as `DATa`, and leaves `value` pointing at the 28-byte string `0x                \xff\xff\xff \xff\xff    `. Bytes in that value tail are not filtered here before they are handed to type-specific parsing.
Case-insensitive dictionary lookup resolves `DATa` to TACACS attribute `Data`, and TACACS autoloads `Data` with type `FR_TYPE_OCTETS`.

fine_trace.code: if (fr_value_box_from_str(vp, &vp->data, vp->da->type, vp->da, value, inlen, quote, tainted) < 0) return -1;
fine_trace.note: Because step 7 resolved the name to `Data`, this conversion call uses `vp->da->type == FR_TYPE_OCTETS`; the 28-byte value tail is therefore parsed as octets instead of being preserved as a generic string.

In the `FR_TYPE_OCTETS` branch, the leading `0x` is recognized, `len` drops from 28 to 26, `ret` becomes 13, and the 26-byte post-prefix tail containing raw `0xff` bytes is handed to `fr_base16_decode()`.

fine_trace.code:
a = fr_is_base16_nstd(p[0], alphabet);
b = fr_is_base16_nstd(p[1], alphabet);
fine_trace.note: As the pairwise base16 loop walks the 26-byte tail from step 9, one of these calls eventually receives `c == 0xff` from the raw value bytes.
Root cause. The selected mixed-case decode alphabet has only `UINT8_MAX` entries, i.e. 255 bytes, so valid indices stop at 254 and there is no in-bounds entry for `0xff`.
Sink. With `c == 0xff`, `(uint8_t)c` becomes 255 and this reads `fr_base16_alphabet_decode_mc[255]`, one byte past the 255-byte global table.

format.name: 79-byte TACACS Authorization RESPONSE whose third `DATa*0x...` argument feeds raw `0xff` bytes to octets/base16 decoding
format.contract: Exactly the staged 79-byte witness in `poc` (sha256 `71d6b9c6e021b03529a022697745d16e7b9e9fb942fdb42ff3cfc6b576ec5bad`). Its verified trigger semantics are: an unencrypted TACACS Authorization RESPONSE (`type 0x02`, even `seq_no 0x20`, 67-byte body) with `arg_cnt = 9` and `data_len = 9`; after the 9-byte argument-length table and the 9-byte `Data` field, the first three declared argument lengths are `0`, `10`, and `33`, so the third argument starts after a 10-byte skip and still ends exactly at the packet end; that third argument is `DATa*0x` followed by 26 post-prefix bytes that still contain raw `0xff`, causing case-insensitive lookup to resolve `DATa` to TACACS `Data`, the `FR_TYPE_OCTETS` parser to strip `0x`, and base16 decoding to reach a `0xff` byte. The later 32-byte lengths present in this witness are not required by the traced sink path.
